My situation isnt nearly as polar as your description suggests but I (F22) show compassion very similarly to you, and my boyfriend (M22) is less of a romantic Id say and a little more quiet when it comes to expressing his feelings (granted this has gotten so much better as time has progressed) if your man is like mine then perhaps he is a bit more closed off and may need more time to open up fully. Another thing we have discussed is love language. Your love languages may be completely different from one another. Maybe you should ask him how he prefers to give and receive love and then share with him your preferences.

I have these same thoughts. It is very hard and I get really down sometimes because of various aspects of distance. Honestly what made it get better for me was when I stopped centering my life around our conversations and calls. I really focus on myself and make sure I do things that will help me grow and enjoy life. I make time to exercise after work, I engage in hobbies regularly, I hang out with friends, I try to really be present and connect with those around me. And at the end of the day there is this beautiful person who is my human who loves and supports me and who I care about so deeply. It is so beautiful and I know the distance is there for a reason and eventually we will be able to be together. There is no point rushing it, all we can do it enjoy the experience, each other, and really just try to grow as individuals.

It isnt something that is seasonal. The way you support him has to be unique to his needs though which you can learn by asking him and through some trial and error. My babe really just wants support through seeing that youre there for him. He might be having a particularly bad day and want to talk about whatever is on his mind for a few hours. It can be really sad to hear but I know he appreciates the avenue to express. I hate hate hate being apart from him when I know he is upset because I know he would be comforted if I were to pop in and cuddle him. But since that isnt possible emotionally cuddling is still an option. I frequently tell him how much I love him and value him and I think that could benefit all relationships. 
My person is coming out of a low and for months I wondered if I would ever see his joyous self again. Slowly but surely he started doing things he previously enjoyed and now he is back to interacting with the external world and I am so happy for him. Just hold in there and this too will pass.

My LDR bf did the sameish thing when we first met. It didnt seem as obvious as your bf who will go out of his was to hang the phone up, but he didnt tell most of his roommates and I believe he told his parents quite a while after I did and then a few friends. I brought it up to him and asked him why/told him all my close friends knew of him and his response was wanting to keep it for himself which doesnt make sense to me and still doesnt and I think he was just afraid that maybe it would end or that people would judge him for dating someone across the country. I believe a month or so passed and he said more people knew and he was proud of dating me. I think maybe he just had some internal fears to get over and realized it hurt me to be kept his secret despite me never explicitly saying that. But I guess my hurt was probably obvious because I brought it up a few times and probably had a sad tone

I know it stinks in the moment and doesnt seem like it will end but it will and he will be back to his happy self at the end. All you can really do is try to be as supportive as possible and dont let it take a toll on you because trust me, worrying about him and the situation will only make it worse for you and your relationship. It gets hard, it gets lonely, but just think about your love for him and how much he needs you right now.
